summary: Round a number with Python’s ties-to-even rule.
documentation: round rounds a number to a requested precision. With no ndigits, rounding a float yields an integer; exact halfway cases choose the even result. Binary floats cannot represent every decimal fraction exactly.
inputs: A number and optional decimal precision.
returns: A rounded value; an integer for float input when precision is omitted.
caution: Do not assume every halfway value rounds upward. Use suitable decimal arithmetic and explicit policy for financial calculations.
scenarios: Create a whole-number display estimate from a measured average.
Round survey measurements consistently for a summary.
Reduce precision in a public statistics table.
title: Round a planning estimate
problem: Input is a number. Return it rounded to the nearest integer using Python round semantics. Tests use integers and exactly representable half-integers; ties go to the even integer.
goal: Use round() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Call round without ndigits; compare 2.5 and 3.5.
